title: Top K by Gap Between Set Bits
statement:
You are given an integer array `arr` and an integer `k`.

For an integer `x`, look at the positions of its set bits (`1` bits) in binary. The **distance** `d(x)` is the **maximum distance between two contiguous (neighbouring) set bits**, measured as the difference of their bit positions. For example, `5` is `101`, whose set bits are at positions 0 and 2, so `d(5) = 2`. For `13 = 1101` the set bits are at positions 0, 2 and 3, the gaps are 2 and 1, so `d(13) = 2`.

If `x` has only one set bit, `d(x) = -1`. The value `0` has no set bits and also has `d(0) = -1`.

Return the **top `k` elements** of `arr` ordered by `d` from largest to smallest. If two elements have the same `d`, the one with the larger decimal value comes first (for instance, if `5` and `6` have the same `d`, then `6` is listed before `5`). Every element of `arr` is a separate candidate, even when values repeat.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers: `arr`.
outputFormat: Print `k` space-separated integers: the chosen elements in the required order.

examples.explanation: The distances are d(5) = 2, d(6) = 1 (110), d(9) = 3 (1001), d(8) = -1 (single set bit) and d(17) = 4 (10001). Sorted by distance: 17, 9, 5, 6, 8, so the top 3 are 17 9 5.
d(5) = 2, d(3) = 1, d(6) = 1, d(12) = 1, d(10) = 2 (1010). The elements with d = 2 come first, larger value first: 10, 5. Then those with d = 1 by larger value: 12, 6, 3. The top 4 are 10 5 12 6.
All four values have d = -1, so they are ordered purely by value, largest first: 4, 2, 1, 0.

hints: First compute d(x) for every element on its own. Walk the bits of x and remember the position of the previous set bit.
The required order is a plain sort on the pair (d, value), both descending.
After sorting, output the first k elements. A heap of size k also works if you want to avoid a full sort.
